home.build: Building Global Careers Through Japanese Education
home.trusted: Trusted Japanese language training for aspiring professionals and future international workers.
home.companyDesc: Our students live with their teachers under a campus with a Japan like environment . They intentionally use the Japanese language, practice the Japanese culture and even practice their skills under a Japanese system
home.proficientDesc: We screen our students well before accepting them into our school. After properly orienting the candidates who pass our screening process, we thoroughly interview them in order to judge their viability for work in Japan
home.provenDesc: Our school operates under a system that makes our students strive for excellence. We give our students monthly written and oral exams, rewarding top students and penalizing under performing students..
home.mannerDesc: Our students learn not only the Japanese language, but they also practice Japanese culture and manners such as proper “Aisatsu” and the importance of always being on time. More over, our students also get to develop their skills by undertaking skills training under a Japanese system.
home.passionateDesc: All of our teachers have worked in Japan for at least 3 years under the TITP and are JLPT (Minimum N3) and JFT Prometric passers. They truly love the company and it can be seen in the way they interact with students, clients and one another. Our teachers are empathetic, honest and passionate, making them the Hashiras of Hashira.
home.well: Well-Known as People Who Work Abroad
home.wellDesc: There are Filipinos all over the world from the United States to the Middle-East and Europe and all across Asia. Filipino workers have been known to be hard-working, bright , friendly and loyal to their employers.
home.englishDesc: Japan is moving towards Globalization and the demand for the English language is growing across the country. Almost all Filipinos are proficient in English and are happy to share their
home.lowAgeDesc: The average age in the Philippines is around 25 years old, which means that there is a lot of youthful energy available for work in an aging Japan
home.lowWageDesc: The minimum wage in the Philippines is around 1,000yen/day. This has driven Filipinos to find employment in foreign countries, with Japan being the top choice for many Filipinos.
home.filipinoLoveDesc: Filipinos are truly enchanted by Japan and its people. We love to watch Anime, sing Karaoke and eat Ramen and Sushi. You probably won’t find a Filipino who doesn’t know what “Arigato” means! Japan is really the dream country of many Filipinos.

corporate.corporateDesc: Know all about one of the Philippines’ leading Japanese Schools
corporate.viceDesc: Nobuaki Kawamichi, Representative, RW Group. He has been involved in the foreign workforce recruitment business since he was 19 years old and participated in launching the business as a founding member of a cross-industry cooperative. Since then, for over 20 years, he has been engaged in the foreign workforce recruitment business, including the Technical Intern Training Program. Currently, as Representative of the RW Group, he oversees foreign talent recruitment, Japanese language education, and various support services. Leveraging his many years of experience and his domestic and international networks, he supports both foreign workers and the companies that hire them. Through the training of foreign workers, Japanese language education, daily life support, and retention support, he is committed to fostering international talent exchange by serving as a bridge connecting Japan and the rest of the world.
corporate.presidentDesc: Joelo is a licensed attorney and a JLPT N1 passer. He obtained his degree in International Business from Pepperdine University and his Juris Doctor from Ateneo De Manila School of Law. He is also the President of Hashira Skills and Language Academy and Pro-Tech Skills Development Center Corporation. He has been with Placewell since 2018.
corporate.missionDesc: To create an inspiring learning environment for students where the Japanese language and culture are practiced daily, leading to their personal development, growth and future success. We hope that the success of our students will lead to more opportunities for Filipinos to work in Japan.
corporate.visionDesc: To make the Filipino the top choice for Japanese companies that need foreign labor. We aim to make our institution one of the prime spots for Filipinos who are looking to find work in Japan.
corporate.ourDesc: We promise that the students that you hire from our school will be ready for work in Japan. They will flourish as workers and be liked as people because of their knowledge of the Japanese Language and respect for the Japanese Culture. We assure you that your Filipino workers will be a great help to you and your company.
corporate.ourStudentDesc: We promise that you will not only gain new and useful knowledge about the Japanese language and culture, but you will also grow as people during your time with us. We will serve you with all our heart because it will be our pleasure to see you fulfill your dreams and succeed in Japan.
corporate.messageDesc: After graduating from college in 2016, I came to Japan to study Japanese language and culture at my mother’s suggestion. My mother believed that, as Japan faced a labor shortage, there was great potential for future talent exchange and business opportunities between the Philippines and Japan. While studying at a Japanese language school, I worked as an English teacher for about six months. However, my true learning journey began after I returned to the Philippines and became involved in launching Placewell International’s Japan-focused business. At first, I faced a series of setbacks and encountered many difficulties. A major challenge was that I lacked a sufficient understanding not only of the Japanese language but also of Japanese workplace culture and business etiquette. Nevertheless, thanks to the warm guidance I received from many Japanese colleagues, I was able to grow by gaining experience step by step. The Philippines is home to many talented individuals capable of succeeding on the global stage. These are people with strong English skills who are diligent, sincere, and contribute to the workplace with a cheerful and positive attitude. Many Filipinos are thriving in countries around the world, and from my own experience, I know that Japan is one of the countries that many young Filipinos aspire to work in. On the other hand, the limited opportunities to receive adequate training in the Japanese language, Japanese culture, and the Japanese workplace present a major challenge for those seeking to work in Japan. Driven by a desire to address these challenges and provide as many Filipinos as possible with the opportunity to thrive in Japan, I founded Hashira Skills. We are committed to nurturing talent capable of smoothly adapting to life and the workplace in Japan by providing thorough instruction not only in the Japanese language but also in Japanese culture, business etiquette, and work ethics. In Japan, as the population ages and birthrates decline, expectations for foreign talent are growing ever higher. We are committed to helping resolve Japan’s labor shortage while supporting the many Filipinos who dream of working in Japan in making their dreams a reality. As a bridge connecting Japanese companies with talented individuals from the Philippines, we sincerely hope to build a better future together with you. We look forward to your continued warm support and guidance.Translated with DeepL.com (free version)

whatIsHashira.title: About Us
whatIsHashira.subtitle: What is Hashira?
whatIsHashira.desc: Filipino workers as the foundation of a Japan in need of labor
whatIsHashira.hashiraDesc: Hashira Skills is a skills and language institution that was established to help young Filipinos achieve their dream of working in Japan. Students live with their teachers in a Japan-like environment where we teach not only the Japanese language but also Japanese culture and manners. Employers can interview candidates who already speak Japanese because we only recommend students for interview if they perform well at school. Hashira Skills prides itself in being an institution that is run by Filipinos who understand the heart of the Japanese.
whatIsHashira.whatDesc: Hashira 柱 is a Japanese language institution that is dedicated to helping Filipinos achieve their dream of working in Japan by providing them with high-quality Japanese language, culture and skills training. Hashira 柱 is the Japanese word for “Pillar” or “Foundation”. Our school was named Hashira 柱 for 2 reasons: “People are the Stones of a Castle” is a Japanese saying that emphasizes the importance of good workers as the foundation of a successful company. Our school is committed to molding workers who will be valuable to any Japanese company. industries.title: About Us
industries.subtitle: Industries
industries.desc: Over 2,000 Filipino workers deployed all across Japan
industries.ourDesc: We provide skilled and dependable Filipino workers to support Japan's growing industries.
industries.constructionDesc: We support a wide range of construction occupations, including carpentry, scaffolding, rebar work, formwork, plastering, painting, and more. We develop workers who have the safety awareness and communication skills required at construction sites in Japan and introduce qualified personnel based on the needs of each company.
industries.shipyardDesc: We support a wide range of welding work, from construction welding to shipyard welding. We have a track record of sending workers to shipbuilding-related companies, including Imabari Shipbuilding and Shin Kurushima Dockyard. We develop personnel equipped with the safety awareness and communication skills required at worksites in Japan.
industries.heavyDesc: We develop personnel qualified for heavy equipment operation and construction machinery-related work. We have a track record of sending workers to construction companies, including Mizutani Construction Co., Ltd., and introduce personnel equipped with strong safety awareness and the ability to respond effectively to on-site requirements.
industries.caregiverDesc: Instruction is provided by teachers with experience working as caregivers in Japan. In addition to Japanese language education, students practically learn the hospitality manners, compassion for users, and communication skills required in caregiving settings, preparing them to succeed as caregivers in Japan.
industries.restoDesc: We have a track record of sending workers to food service companies, including CoCo Ichibanya, KFC, and Shakey's. Students learn customer service manners, hygiene management, and the spirit of Japanese hospitality, preparing them to succeed in Japan's food service industry.
industries.factoryDesc: We support a wide range of manufacturing industries, including food production, machining, metal processing, and electronic component manufacturing. Our training emphasizes safety awareness, quality control, and teamwork, developing personnel who can succeed in Japan's manufacturing industry.
industries.farmerDesc: We have a track record of sending workers to agriculture-related companies, including Iwai Ryutsu Co., Ltd. and Kunizaki Seika Co., Ltd. Workers are trained for tasks such as growing, harvesting, sorting, and shipping vegetables and fruits, preparing them to succeed in Japan's agricultural industry.
industries.hotelDesc: We have a track record of sending workers to accommodation and tourism-related companies, including Terrace Hotels Co., Ltd. Students learn customer service manners and the spirit of Japanese hospitality, preparing them to succeed in Japan's hotel industry.
industries.map: Track Record of Sending Workers Across Japan
industries.explore: We introduce the areas across Japan where we have a track record of sending workers. Filipino workers are active in various regions and industries, supporting many companies.

overall.title: System
overall.subtitle: Overall
overall.desc: Our system ensures that we provide our clients with the best possible Filipino Workers
overall.OrientationDesc: We start by hosting an information session for interested candidates where we explain the whole process from point A to Z.
overall.ScreeningDesc: Candidates who are interested in our program are pre-interviewed and screened through IQ, math, and personality tests and more.
overall.StudyDesc: Employers can interview candidates who already speak Japanese because we only recommend students for interview if they perform well at school.
overall.InterviewDesc: We are able to facilitate orderly and efficient interviews and trade tests through our experienced staff.
overall.MonthlyDesc: Our students are required to take a monthly evaluation. Those who fail are either kicked out or re-batched.
overall.PostDesc: Although it is mainly the responsibility of the agency to monitor our workers in Japan, we take responsibility in ensuring the welfare of our students in Japan because we treasure the relationship we built with them while they studied at our school.

specialRules.title: System
specialRules.subtitle: Special Rules
specialRules.desc: We implement these rules to encourage a disciplined and competitive environment
specialRules.JapaneseDesc: We encourage our students to speak Japanese as much as possible while inside the school.
specialRules.StrikeDesc: Students who break rules and consistently perform poorly in class may be subjected to warnings or even dismissal from the school.
specialRules.MockDesc: Our students are required to take multiple JFT mock tests before taking the actual exam. Our mock tests consist of compilations of past JFT questions.
specialRules.WeekendDesc: Students are allowed to go home for the weekend if their cumulative average for the said week is above 70%.
specialRules.RebatchingDesc: We give chances to failing students who have a good attitude and work hard. Instead of kicking them out, we transfer them to a lower batch in hopes they give an improved performance.

construction.title: Skills Training
construction.subtitle: Construction
construction.desc: See how we train our construction workers
construction.WeldingDesc: Learn the fundamental knowledge, safety procedures, and practical skills required for welding work. Our training prepares students for manufacturing and construction workplaces in Japan.
construction.CarpentryDesc: Students learn basic construction techniques, tool handling, and workplace safety to develop the skills needed in Japan's building industry.
construction.ScaffoldingDesc: Training focuses on scaffolding assembly, dismantling procedures, safety awareness, and teamwork required on Japanese construction sites.
construction.MasonryDesc: Students learn the fundamentals of plastering work, including material handling, finishing techniques, and quality control standards.
construction.PaintingDesc: Our painting program covers surface preparation, painting techniques, and safety practices to help students succeed in Japanese workplaces.
construction.SafetyDesc: We believe that safety is the foundation of every successful worker. Through continuous guidance and practical training, we instill strong safety awareness and responsible workplace behavior in our students.
construction.TechnicalDesc: Effective communication begins with understanding the language of the workplace. We provide industry-specific terminology training to help students communicate confidently and accurately in Japan.
construction.EmphasisDesc: Understanding instructions correctly is essential for success in the workplace. Our training focuses on developing listening, comprehension, and response skills needed in Japanese working environments.
construction.bottomSubtitle: We also offer special lessons on Japanese culture!

hospitality.title: Skills Training
hospitality.subtitle: Hospitality
hospitality.desc: Enhancing the heart of the Filipino
hospitality.CaregivingDesc: Our caregiving training facility is designed to simulate a modern Japanese nursing care environment. Students develop practical skills, professional knowledge, and the mindset required to provide compassionate care in Japan.
hospitality.FoodDesc: Students receive hands-on training in food preparation, customer service, hygiene management, and workplace communication to meet the standards of Japan's food service industry.
hospitality.HousekeepingDesc: Our training environment replicates hotel and residential settings, allowing students to develop cleaning, organization, and hospitality skills required in Japan.
hospitality.JapaneseDesc: We will learn Japan’s unique spirit of “omotenashi” and cultivate a considerate attitude, attentiveness, and good manners. Our goal is to provide services that satisfy our clients and customers.
hospitality.TechnicalDesc: Students will learn the honorific language and technical terms used in the service industry and develop the communication skills necessary to interact with customers and clients in an appropriate and courteous manner.
hospitality.bottomSubtitle: We also offer special lessons on Japanese culture!

japaneseCulture.title: System
japaneseCulture.subtitle: Japanese Culture and Manners
japaneseCulture.desc: Just as important as Japanese language
japaneseCulture.item1Desc: Learn about Japanese culture, daily customs, workplace etiquette, and rules to help you adapt smoothly to life and work in Japan.
japaneseCulture.item2Desc: Develop the habit of proper greetings, an important part of Japanese society, and build communication skills that create a positive impression.
japaneseCulture.item3Desc: Through dormitory living designed to simulate communal life in Japan, students develop discipline, teamwork, cleanliness, and a sense of responsibility.
japaneseCulture.item4Desc: Learn proper waste separation methods and recycling rules that are essential to daily life in Japan while developing greater environmental awareness.
japaneseCulture.item5Desc: Former technical interns with work experience in Japan provide practical advice and guidance based on their own experiences.

slide2.Through: Through Japanese language instruction, specialized education, and life guidance,

whatIsHashiraItem.item1Desc: Learn comprehensively about Japanese culture and customs, daily life etiquette in Japan, seasonal events, and traditional culture to deepen your understanding of Japanese society.
whatIsHashiraItem.item2Desc: Learn practical Japanese communication skills for daily and workplace conversations, including honorifics, reporting, contacting, consulting, and customer service expressions.
whatIsHashiraItem.item3Desc: Understand Japanese ways of thinking and values while learning practical workplace attitudes, sense of responsibility, cooperation, courtesy, and time awareness.
whatIsHashiraItem.item4Desc: Through pre-interview training, students develop basic Japanese language skills before the interview and gain the confidence to participate in company interviews in Japanese.
whatIsHashiraItem.item5Desc: Our staff help students understand the mindset and way of thinking of Japanese people while providing guidance that addresses the concerns and challenges faced by Filipino students.
whatIsHashiraItem.item6Desc: Students live together in an environment that simulates life in Japan, allowing them to practically learn Japanese lifestyles, culture, and etiquette while developing the skills needed to adapt smoothly to life in Japan.

schoolInformation.section3Subtitle: We support your first step toward success in Japan with an environment designed for both comfortable learning and living.
schoolInformation.item1Desc: Every morning, all students participate in exercises and a morning assembly to start the day with energy and enthusiasm.
schoolInformation.item2Desc: The cafeteria provides nutritionally balanced meals, while students become accustomed to life in Japan through practicing meals using chopsticks.
schoolInformation.item3Desc: Our TESDA-certified welding practice area allows candidates' practical skills to be assessed on-site, making it possible to evaluate their technical abilities during interviews.
schoolInformation.item4Desc: Bright and comfortable classrooms provide an environment where students can focus on learning Japanese and developing specialized knowledge.
schoolInformation.item5Desc: Experienced instructors are always available to provide support and guidance regarding students' learning and daily life.
schoolInformation.item6Desc: Equipped with a stable internet connection, the interview room accommodates both online and face-to-face interviews.
schoolInformation.item7Desc: Our full-dormitory environment allows students to live safely and securely while focusing on their studies. Through communal living, students also develop the lifestyle habits and teamwork skills needed in Japan.
schoolInformation.item8Desc: By doing their own laundry every day, students develop independence and essential life skills.

groupCompany.title: Company Introduction
groupCompany.subtitle: Introduction to Our Group Companies
groupCompany.desc: An introduction to our group companies
groupCompany.item1Desc: Placewell International is a Filipino-owned, family-run manpower agency that has been sending Filipino workers overseas for more than 50 years. Headquartered in Makati, the company works with more than 15 branches nationwide to recruit, train, and deploy Filipino talent to companies around the world. Placewell is committed to providing reliable talent and efficient, organized, and responsive services, while also creating opportunities for professional growth by connecting Filipino workers with companies that recognize and value their contributions.
groupCompany.item2Desc: Sky Innovation is a recruitment agency specializing in services for Japanese clients. Our staff specializes in accompanying clients on business trips to the Philippines, providing interpretation and facilitating interviews, and preparing documents related to the MWO, OTIT, and immigration authorities.
groupCompany.item3Desc: Like Hashira Skills, Protec Skills is a TESDA-accredited vocational and language training center. At Protec, you can study courses in the fields of nursing care, housekeeping, and the foodservice industry. We used to offer Japanese language classes as well, but since our group transitioned to a shared-living system, we no longer offer them.
